We’re thrilled to announce the launch of our Delegators Reward Program, an opportunity for you to support the WorldMapPin project while earning rewards simultaneously. This is another big step in the evolution of this great project that we all love. ### How It All Started The idea popped out during a delightful breakfast at Hivefest when @roelandp asked @detlev and @lizanomadsoul if we had a plan about rewarding our delegators. Since then, we've put a lot of thought into creating a program that not only rewards you, our amazing supporters but also strengthens the Hive ecosystem. Big thank you to @arcange for coding and testing the system for the project. ### Why a Delegators Reward Program? The program aims at rewarding anyone who delegates at least 50 HP to @worldmappin in order to give back as a thank-you for their delegation. By delegating Hive Power to @worldmappin, you become an integral part of our project, supporting the curation of daily travel content and receiving a share of the curation rewards proportional to your delegation. The @worldmappin team curates travel content daily and votes for the best English and Spanish posts. Our curation rewards are quite high as we are very active in curating quality content. Our average curation APR ranges from 9% to 11%, which our delegators will also benefit from. ### How does it work? Several other projects on HIVE reward their delegators with HIVE, HBD, or with their own tokens. At @worldmappin, we have decided to reward our delegators with Hive Power (HP). The main reasons to do so are: - We will grow together - If you were doing your own curation, you would also receive Hive Power - It is a healthy way to support the Hive Eco System. We will share 80% of our curation rewards with our delegator. The remaining will be used to grow the @worldmappin account and provide greater rewards to the talented authors we curate. *Note: for efficiency reasons, we will not distribute a reward if its amount is less than 0.005 HP. With a delegation of at least 50 HP, this should not be an issue.* ### When? Our Delegators Reward Program will start on **November 1st**! This means we will collect data on curation rewards and delegations once the day is over. Only after that our delegators will receive their rewards. [Léelo en **español** aquí](#spanish)
![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EphwvnseGpoFsqerip5DYGfvbjMnpcP2dKvEaiP5Ezhaad1uqpdt9YswSrDWH917stk.jpg) # Our goal at Worldmappin Map and Travel Community Since **the worldmappin.com map** exists we have planned to extend it for all Hive users, which means everyone can pin their post on the map and link it to the content-related community - bringing all the users and communities together in one place again the worldmappin.com map. **The Worldmappin Community** is the start of showing how that works. It always has been and will be travel-related, because our vision in this **community** has always been two things: A: Provide each traveler with their unique world map, where they can explore the world, pin their trips and memories, and dive back into the memories whenever they want with just a click. B: Give the travelers a platform to share their adventures and experiences with others, so that the whole community benefits from using the map as a travel guide to finding more information and inspiration for their next trips. As you know the curation team of @worldmappin project: @lizanomadsoul, @ybanezkim26, @lauramica, @glecerioberto, and @ninaeatshere, is checking the incoming travel posts of this community every day, curating the top content and giving the winners visibility in our Daily Travel Digest. We often get questions from our community members on what to do and not do, or how they can improve their content to get curated by our team. So we took some time within the team to write down our guidelines with all the rules and suggestions, on which you can rely when writing a travel post within the @Worldmappin community. In this post, we will go into detail about every one of them. - Thanks also to @livinguktaiwan and the rest of the @worldmappin team @detlev, @arcange, @godfish,@louis88, @rivalzzz, @masterswatch and @uniforced for your input and for the support on this. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 19.17.17.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23w3EVhVkZqLVzF3s3wB8HBA6aoHDSZnwZ4rjrPDKzQj9Gi5wqtBKyYnjq4EQXm7J79wT.png) For us, it is important, that all of you have the same knowledge and possibilities to position your content within this community following the standards of quality that we seek to ensure following our vision. ![Authorized picture by @bil.prag](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23tvkkLbUnByuUE82pY5LHSVDy7hfUmnA9fEPDvhmPzSGJBpQPekoqp9yUjqtax4CrvFY.jpeg) # Intro We love and celebrate the huge diversity in our community, representing different cultures, customs, mentalities, genders, age groups, and languages. Every traveler has his/her unique character, perception of the world, values, and strengths that make him/her the special person that we love to follow on their trips. We are very aware that with this uniqueness there comes different styles of writing, taking pictures or telling a story and that is super great! So of course, this summary is meant only as a suggestion! We love and understand that HIVE is a decentralized ecosystem, where we are all free to create content in our own individual way! However, if you share our goal and want to get support for your efforts, you may want to consider certain rules and suggestions for your future posts, that allow us to establish a standard of quality. # So let's get started! Read further and get more clear on these things on the way! ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23xoueMQMECcMBErfM1aCGiDLJkg2Y2xcvtwnRnCg7WA5SBVSsTeKdAvV1teUt7yv6q75.jpg) ## Rules for posting in the community As you may know, every community has its own rules. The rules are our most important guidelines to follow our vision and keep the quality for every one of you. If you want to be in this community you have to follow them, otherwise you will be muted at some point. Those rules have been implemented since the beginning of the project and are regularly updated. ### Rule Nr. 1. This community is only for posts included in the https://worldmappin.com map. The most important rule of our community is to pin your post to our map, because for us it's not only important that you can collect your posts on your map, but also that other travelers can benefit from your experiences. Of course, this will also give your post more exposure, as well as a chance to be featured in our daily Travel Digest 😃. There are two ways to pin your post to the map: - Include PINs from PeakD: After writing your post, click on the map icon at the bottom. It's next to “ Short preview description” and above the “Advanced” icon. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.00.51.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/Eo6SchkLfuZGRfoyFcwgv3N2WiVnFNP38U8cifkis662bFNF1j2PzpwdcYQDjD7Amhq.png) - Include PINs in the rest of the Front-ends: - Go to https://worldmappin.com/ - Find the location of your publication on the map, you can do this by scrolling the map or using the search bar. - Click on the GET CODE button and then click on the exact location of your publication: a code snippet will be generated. - Copy the code and paste it into the draft of your Hive post. Then publish it. 🙂 - The code will be invisible in your post, but a few minutes after publishing you will receive a comment informing you that your post has been added to the map. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.01.24.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23wgUJT7kkrRyKQsXSLrRbivrgJ18h3sPeyGJVnZFTJDV8H1Xco8EN1zcJdXtpDQrCQUo.png) ### Rule Nr. 2. English and Spanish content only. (or bi-lingual with one of the languages being English or Spanish) As we want this map to be understandable for most of our users and we are still growing. We only allow English or Spanish content for now. Of course we plan to extend this rule to more languages over time but for now only those two languages are allowed and being curated. If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language next to the English or Spanish text. ### Rule Nr. 3. Only original content, no plagiarism, no AI-generated content, no recycled content. We want to know what you experienced! See your Pictures and get shared your personal knowledge - so we can be on the trip together and follow your adventures just the way you did! So please only use information, pictures, or videos that are yours (or put the source). Plagiarism is not allowed because of obvious reasons. We know that AI is the future, it is fun and that of course it can help put more value on your post sometimes, but there are also some users out there, who are writing their posts using AI only - trying to use it only to get some payout - not to share their trip experiences with others. So for us, a mix is ok, but we will know if it is 100% AI generated and that is fully against our rules as it is also not you - and therefore not following our vision and values. Recycling old posts and pictures same as writing multiple times about the same place /the same experience is not allowed for the same reasons. ### Rule Nr. 4. Content must be about places you have personally traveled to and about your experience. We want you to explore your own map, make your own experiences and share them with the community, so they get inspired to do something like that as well! We love to be on your side when you are getting out of your comfort zone, taking on new adventures and checking out new places. So don´t just plan it theoretically - go, do it, and write about it after you experience it yourself! ### Rule Nr. 5. Worldmappin is a travel community, please post reviews of accommodations, food, and restaurants in other appropriate communities. Please avoid posting on unrelated topics. This also includes - reviews about accommodations - shopping malls - restaurants - tips & tricks on transportation unless they are only a small part of your trip and not the main topic of the post OR such a place of interest to travel to, because of historic /extra cool background. However, you can pin your posts from other communities on the map, to keep track of all your visits on https://worldmappin.com. Here are some examples (click on each image to see details): |[Actifit community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-193552/created) |[BEER community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-187719/created) |[HiveFest community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-106258/created)| |-|-|-| |
[![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://usermedia.actifit.io/D9DCB68D-D042-45C3-80E3-739DF4AE1581638640735517426688)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@ninaeatshere/actifit-ninaeatshere-20241009t182346898z)
|
[![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbpc9YajQkcxGv9kMtTkGGXMLfq3B4WSTKiriGbKDXBXz/img_3344.jpg)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@ninaeatshere/beer-tasting-at-hivefest-split)
| [![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoGyotE2GeJxou8KqraF6yzEnaPDAYshQ2Q4njiwdHRzCKxJCNQdauwGysDMKm9XWzx.jpeg)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@ninaeatshere/restaurant-gusar-hivefest-gala-dinner-or-engesp) | | [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eo2BSgYeWqHyJeFCtZdKFTZdQcDyUJUersW5YPavQEspAyECJkZbG9sjAc6m2noLD6i.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@worldmappin/wmp1728499187646)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbkj8CLsRWaYya87AmM3xbgqg1UYTcLfvycps5qRkU18MhVUwRfMvGWquhuWrVmesi.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@worldmappin/wmp1727017768292)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbg1MP4BtYk2Qt8dEtzJ46Ld83kwSwpzMEZVNeGrJD9ojyvgMQpVyPsqFFjQJ9HmH6.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@worldmappin/wmp1726526214980)| ### Rule Nr. 6. Penalties that happen if you don´t follow the rules If you don´t follow our community rules, you will be muted. Depending on which rule you are breaking, you get a warning and will be watched or muted right away. As the general consensus within Hive is that plagiarized content, AI-generated, spam, and recycled posts meant to farm rewards are to be muted, and users involved in those activities are to be penalized by blacklisting from further curation, here we are very strict and act right away. If you break one of the other rules you will get a friendly reminder and will be put on our watchlist. If it happens again you will be muted again. - If you are having trouble with this or you have questions on it you can get in touch with us on [Discord Channel](https://discord.gg/EGtBvSM) at any time. ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EqBbJbYvcJYiErfDBaRHrRiwc7M95b4LRZV3u1CUZwZRuQR1MDpFsiiZEcvbCSTrTqv.jpeg) ## Suggestions Congrats! You have made it through the rule jungle and are enjoying the view as all the fog should be gone by now. As a big thank you for your attention and because you are a great member of this community, we want to give you a small collection of suggestions to make your content even more exciting for others to read. Of course, those things can also help to be selected by us in the daily Traveldigest. ### Headline of the post On Hive, hundreds of posts are published every day, so it is very difficult for curators to cover all the content. The title we choose is the first piece of information we see from your work, so it is important that the title of your post is short, attractive, and related to the content you submit. There is no single way, but in terms of travel content, it is advisable to indicate the location or the name of the place you visit instead or in addition to your invitation to read the content of an adventure. It is recommended to avoid long titles, there is just no need to detail itineraries or exalt the headline, so get to the point 😎. ### Bilingual posts As we told you already in the rules section: If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language. This helps us to verify the authenticity of the text and allows you to have a wider audience and interactions with people who also speak the same language as you. Of course, always include the English translation. When you do so, please make it visually attractive and easy to follow. As for the way to distribute the content in different languages, there are many possibilities (one language first followed by the other, translation by blocks of content or in different columns, among others) and all of them are valid, the important thing is that the way you present it allows the reader to feel comfortable when reading your content. Try to put yourself on the reader's side. As for the **title**, try to point out the languages in which it is available, no need to be redundant. Here are some examples, there can be many variations of this, but the best is to indicate only once in the sentence the presence of each language: *e.g.1 “My post headline [Eng][Esp]” e.g.2 “El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]” e.g.3 “My post headline | El título de mi post”*. ### Length of content Travel and adventure are words that by themselves open our imagination to countless stories. Remember that our goal in this community is to invite others to accompany us during the travels and serve as a guide to visit. You write about your experiences and let others know about the spots you have enjoyed the most. It is difficult to summarize them in just 300 words. Of course you can, but is it enough to make your experience the best of the day? By this, we don't mean that we write a lot just to increase volume, nor that your publications have to be full of historical/technical data obtained from other sources. What we love is for you to take us on a journey with you, with your emotions and sensations through the journey that many can make, but that has been unique for you. The moment you to tell us your own story, what particularly inspired you to talk about it, it is not difficult to reach **at least 500 words**, which could be considered as a starting point to stand out. ![Authorized gif by @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xVMRr2moLd8z8im7sHAq2k8EfG9PfHVPrcL9fZG5vGYtn18KNTspFHUgTZai8xPZed6.gif) ### Photos and videos This is another important feature that immediately captures the reader's attention. Choosing and highlighting your images can be crucial when promoting your publication, but you must not forget that the essence of a travel post is your story, the experience, and the anecdotes that allow you to capture those moments with which you illustrate your blog. We recommend finding a balance between photos and text. You can use as many photos as you want, but remember that these serve as backup to your story, this community is not about photography, so publishing 20 photos and 100 words, is not as interesting as a travel guide. On the other side sharing only 3 images that do not highlight that incredible journey is also not telling so much about your adventure. Therefore, a basic recommendation would be to include at least 5 photos of the environment we visited, showing the landscape, the town, or the monuments. Taking pictures of ourselves during the tour, selfies, and photos of food and lodging is super nice to see, but cannot be the main part of the audiovisual material, remember that the community is focused on the traveler's destination. Try to take care of the quality of the photographs. Lack of focus and leaning without seeking dynamism or any other form of artistic expression, end up in images that are difficult to understand. As for **the videos, regardless of the length, there is no justifying the lack of text and images** sharing our experience. Not everyone has the time to watch a whole video, the best thing is to offer the viewer both options so that we not only have video views but also invite readers to enjoy our experience. We recommend orienting the device used for recording horizontally so that it is more friendly to the eye in 3Speak. ### Sources, quotations, rights, and credits We have emphasized the importance of sharing original content, based on personal experience and according to rules 3 and 4 of the community, so it might go without saying that the text, images, and other resources used in the publication must be our own. However, for specific occasions within the post, when we share an image or video **authorized** by third parties, we must give credit to the authors and link to the source link to verify its veracity. This is not a problem if we do not base our entire article on someone else's reference, but we introduce an element to improve the story we have been sharing with others. ### Tags In any case, in Hive tags must be related to the content you are writing about. Within the community, we don't require any in particular, but #Travel will help you classify your content, making it more accessible when someone is interested in this topic. Some relevant monuments or features of the place visited are #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. If you include a language other than English, use the tag of your language of origin and some reference to travel (e.g. #Spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Authorized picture by @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Engagement Last but not least, as important as all the previous sections, the commitment of each user within the blockchain and especially in the community is fundamental. Has conseguido atravesar la jungla de reglas y estás disfrutando de la vista, ya que toda la niebla debería haberse disipado ya. Como gran agradecimiento por tu atención y porque eres un gran miembro de esta comunidad, queremos darte una pequeña colección de sugerencias para que tu contenido sea aún más emocionante de leer para los demás. Por supuesto, esas cosas también pueden ayudar a ser seleccionado por nosotros en el Traveldigest diario. ### Título del post En Hive se publican cientos de posts cada día, por lo que es muy difícil para los curadores abarcar todo el contenido. El título que elegimos es la primera información que vemos de tu trabajo, por lo que es importante que el título de tu publicación sea corto, atractivo y esté relacionado con el contenido que presentas. No hay una forma única, pero en términos de contenido de viaje, es aconsejable indicar la ubicación o el nombre del lugar que visitas en vez, o además, de tu invitación a leer el contenido de una aventura. Se recomienda evitar los títulos largos, no hace falta detallar itinerarios ni exaltar el título, así que ve al grano 😎. ### Publicaciones bilingües Como ya te dijimos en la sección de normas: Si tu lengua materna no es el inglés, no dudes en incluir la versión original de tu escrito en tu lengua de origen. Esto nos ayuda a verificar la autenticidad del texto y te permite tener una audiencia más amplia e interactuar con personas que también hablan el mismo idioma que tú. Por supuesto, incluye siempre la traducción al inglés. Cuando lo hagas, procura que sea visualmente atractivo y fácil de seguir. En cuanto a la forma de distribuir el contenido en diferentes idiomas, hay muchas posibilidades (un idioma primero seguido del otro, traducción por bloques de contenido o en diferentes columnas, entre otras) y todas son válidas, lo importante es que la forma en que lo presentes permita al lector sentirse cómodo al momento de leer tu contenido. Intenta ponerte en el lugar del lector. En cuanto al **título**, intenta señalar los idiomas en los que está disponible, no hace falta ser redundante. He aquí algunos ejemplos, puede haber muchas variantes, pero lo mejor es indicar una sola vez en la frase la presencia de cada idioma: *e. j.1 "El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]" e. j. 2 "My post headline [Eng][Esp]" e. j. 3 "El título de mi post | My post headline"*. ### Extensión del contenido Viaje y aventura son palabras que por sí solas despiertan nuestra imaginación a innumerables historias. Recuerda que nuestro objetivo en esta comunidad es invitar a otros a acompañarnos durante los viajes y servir de guía para su visita. Escribe sobre tus experiencias y da a conocer a los demás los lugares que más te han gustado. Es difícil resumirlos en sólo 300 palabras. Claro que puedes, pero ¿es suficiente para que tu experiencia sea la mejor de todas a lo largo del día? Con esto no queremos decir que escribas mucho sólo para incrementar el volumen, ni que tus publicaciones tengan que estar llenas de datos históricos/técnicos obtenidos de otras fuentes. Lo que nos encanta es que nos lleves de viaje contigo, con tus emociones y sensaciones a través del recorrido que muchos pueden hacer, pero que para ti ha sido único. En el momento en que nos cuentes tu propia historia, lo que te ha inspirado especialmente para hablar de ello, no es difícil llegar a **al menos 500 palabras**, lo que podría considerarse como un punto de partida para sobresalir. ![Gif autorizado por @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/241tQTPAaoSvjN9G5z3mBNQS3XaSMPsPBceZbR5WwdZXYC9pHGsm2VAdJwwrLX1icFiib.gif) ### Fotos y vídeos Este es otro elemento importante que capta inmediatamente la atención del lector. Elegir y destacar tus imágenes puede ser crucial a la hora de promocionar tu publicación, pero no debes olvidar que la esencia de un post de viajes es tu historia, la experiencia y las anécdotas que te permiten capturar esos momentos con los que ilustras tu blog. Te recomendamos que encuentres un equilibrio entre fotos y texto. Puedes utilizar todas las fotos que quieras, pero recuerda que éstas sirven de respaldo a tu historia, esta comunidad no es de fotografía, por lo que publicar 20 fotos y 100 palabras, no es tan interesante para una guía de viajes. Por otro lado compartir solo 3 imágenes que no resalten aquel increíble viaje tampoco está contando mucho sobre tu aventura. Por lo tanto, una recomendación básica sería incluir al menos 5 fotos del entorno que visitamos, mostrando el paisaje, el pueblo, o los monuments. Hacernos fotos durante el recorrido, selfies, fotos de la comida y el alojamiento es súper agradable de ver, pero no puede ser la parte principal del material audiovisual, recuerda que la comunidad se centra en el destino del viajero. Trata de cuidar la calidad de las fotografías. La falta de enfoque y el inclinarlas, sin buscar dinamismo o cualquier otra forma de expresión artística, acaban en imágenes difíciles de entender. En cuanto a **los vídeos, independientemente de su duración, no se justifica la falta de texto e imágenes** compartiendo nuestra experiencia. No todo el mundo tiene tiempo de ver un vídeo entero, lo mejor es ofrecer al espectador las dos opciones, para que no sólo tengamos visualizaciones del vídeo, sino que invitemos a los lectores a disfrutar de nuestra experiencia. Te recomendamos orientar el dispositivo utilizado para la grabación en horizontal, para que sea más amigable a la vista en 3Speak. ### Fuentes, citas, derechos y créditos Hemos hecho hincapié en la importancia de compartir contenido original, basado en la experiencia personal y de acuerdo con las reglas 3 y 4 de la comunidad, por lo que puede que no haga falta decir que el texto, las imágenes y otros recursos utilizados en la publicación deben ser propios. Sin embargo, en ocasiones puntuales dentro del post, cuando compartamos una imagen o vídeo **autorizado** por terceros, deberemos dar crédito a los autores y enlazar al link de la fuente para comprobar su veracidad. Esto no es un problema si no basamos todo nuestro artículo en la referencia de otra persona, sino que introducimos un elemento para mejorar la historia que hemos compartido con los demás. ### Etiquetas En todo momento, las etiquetas en Hive deben estar relacionadas con el contenido sobre el que escribes. Dentro de la comunidad, no exigimos ninguna en particular, pero #Travel te ayudará a clasificar tu contenido, haciéndolo más accesible cuando alguien se interese por este tema. Lo mismo ocurre cuando incluyes en las etiquetas la ciudad, el país o la región que estás visitando. También puedes utilizar referencias a la forma de viajar, #backpacking, #roadtrip, #solotravel, #hiking, entre otras. Algunos monumentos o características relevantes del lugar visitado son #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. Sólo para facilitar la búsqueda de contenidos similares, en caso de que alguien se interese por el artículo debido a esa mención concreta. En definitiva, aquí buscamos compartir nuestra pasión por viajar: #wanderlust. Si incluyes un idioma que no sea el inglés, utiliza la etiqueta de tu idioma de origen y alguna referencia a los viajes (por ejemplo, #spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Foto autorizada por @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Compromiso Por último, tan importante como todos los apartados anteriores, es fundamental el compromiso de cada usuario dentro de la blockchain y especialmente en la comunidad. Si esperamos recibir apoyo, lo más razonable es apoyar a los creadores de contenido que hacen el mismo esfuerzo que nosotros y que dan vida a nuestro universo viajero. Ser un miembro activo de una comunidad no significa sólo publicar en ella, sino interactuar con otros usuarios en las publicaciones de la comunidad más allá de responder a los comentarios de nuestros posts. Votar, comentar y aportar opiniones son formas de apoyarnos mutuamente, compartir experiencias, ponernos en contacto, hacer nuevas amistades y, por supuesto, aprender y añadir valor real al ecosistema. I like it when memorable outings come up during a trip, and I was sure that would happen once I reunited with my friend Noe in Paraguay. We had both had a great experience during our volunteer work in Salta, Argentina, and I was hoping the same would happen while we explored Asunción. Since she had already been in the city for over a month, she moved around the streets comfortably, which was helpful for me to have an almost-local guide and to discover places I wouldn’t have visited on my own 😃.
Me gusta cuando en el viaje surgen paseos memorables y estaba segura de que eso pasaría una vez que me reencontrara con mi amiga Noe en Paraguay. Las dos habíamos tenido una grata experiencia durante nuestro voluntariado en Salta, Argentina, y esperaba que pasara lo mismo mientras visitábamos Asunción. Como ella ya llevaba más de un mes en la ciudad, ya se manejaba cómodamente en las calles, lo que a mí me sirvió para tener una guía casi local, y para descubrir lugares que sola no hubiese visitado 😃.
--- ---
--- --- One of the afternoons I was walking around Asunción, Noe told me about a bar she wanted us to visit. She hadn’t been there before, so she thought it would be a good idea to discover it together. As usual, I don’t really pay much attention to where we’re going—I just trust my guide at the time and start walking. Since Asunción is a big city, I knew we would be walking quite a bit, so I put on comfortable clothes and we headed toward an area called Loma de San Jerónimo.
Una de las tardes que estuve paseando por Asunción, Noe me comentó sobre un bar que quería que visitemos. Ella no lo conocía, así que pensó que sería buena idea descubrirlo juntas. Como siempre, yo nunca me fijo muy bien hacia donde vamos: solo confío en mi guía de turno y empiezo a caminar. Como Asunción es una ciudad grande, supe que caminaríamos bastante, así que me puse ropa cómoda y salimos hacia una zona llamada Loma de San Gerónimo.
---
--- Big cities have their beautiful sides, but also their less touristy areas, and I admit that when I saw we were getting quite far from the center, I got a bit scared. I was even more uneasy when we started looking for the bar in a neighborhood full of small passageways and staircases. Everything looked very picturesque and well-kept, but at the same time it was quiet and almost empty. I’m not very brave when it comes to possible insecurity, but I tried not to think about it and just enjoy the walk while Noe tried to guide us to the bar through that maze.
Las ciudades grandes tienen sus partes lindas pero también tienen sus partes no tan turísticas, y admito que cuando vi que nos estábamos alejando bastante del centro me asusté un poco. Y más aún me asusté cuando empezamos a buscar el bar dentro de un barrio lleno de pequeños pasillos y escaleras. Todo se veía muy pintoresco y bien cuidado, pero a la vez silencioso y casi sin gente. Yo no soy nada valiente frente a la posible inseguridad, pero traté de no pensar en eso y disfrutar el paseo mientras Noe intentaba guiarnos hasta el bar entre todo ese laberinto.
---
---
---
---
--- After walking for quite a while and finally accepting that we had gotten lost, Noe and I found a small store that was open and asked if there really was a bar in that area. It was a relief to know there was and to receive clear directions on how to get there. It turned out the bar was located on the terrace of a house, just a few passageways away from where we were at that moment. We both found it strange what kind of bar it would be in such a hard-to-reach place, but it was a pleasant surprise to discover that it did exist and was even more beautiful than we had imagined.
Después de caminar un buen rato y finalmente aceptar que nos habíamos perdido, Noe y yo encontramos un almacén abierto y preguntamos si efectivamente había un bar en esa zona. Nos alivió saber que si y recibir indicaciones precisas sobre cómo llegar a él. Resultó que el bar se encontraba en la terraza de una casa, a unos cuantos pasillos de donde estábamos en ese momento. A las dos nos resultaba raro el tipo de bar que sería en este lugar tan complicado para llegar, pero fue una buena sorpresa descubrir que efectivamente el lugar existía y era más hermoso de lo que pensábamos.
---
--- Since we had visited this place during siesta time, it wasn’t open when we arrived, but the owner kindly opened the door for us and let us in. We were surprised by the trust he placed in us, because all the drinks at the bar were available and he simply left us there alone to enjoy the space. Everything looked very new and beautiful, as picturesque as the neighborhood below. It would have been great to see it open and at night, but I wasn’t sure if I wanted to walk through those passageways later on.
Como habíamos visitado este lugar en la hora de la siesta, no estaba abierto para cuando llegamos, pero su dueño amablemente nos abrió la puerta y nos dejó pasar. Nos sorprendió la confianza que nos tuvo, porque todas las bebidas del bar estaban a disposición y él simplemente nos dejó ahí solas disfrutando del espacio. Todo se veía muy nuevo y lindo, pintoresco como el barrio más abajo. Hubiese sido genial verlo abierto y de noche, pero no estaba segura de si quería caminar en esos pasillos más tarde.
---
--- Without a doubt, the best part of this bar was the beautiful views of the city. Being a bit elevated already allowed you to see Asunción from above. The afternoon was lovely, and we stayed for quite a while taking photos, as well as charging our phones to continue with the outing. By then, all the adrenaline I had built up on the way there was starting to fade, and I was able to relax after the successful adventure. Deep down, I knew Noe wouldn’t get us into trouble 😂.
Sin dudas, la mejor parte de este bar eran las hermosas vistas de la ciudad. Estar un poco en altura ya te permitía ver Asunción desde lo alto. La tarde estaba hermosa, y nos quedamos un buen rato haciendo una sesión de fotos, además de cargando nuestros celulares para continuar con el paseo. Para entonces, toda la adrenalina que había acumulado en el trayecto de ida ya se estaba disolviendo, y puse relajarme frente al paseo exitoso. En el fondo sabía que Noe no iba a meternos en problemas 😂.
---
--- Visiting this bar, called Guaraní Lounge, was a great memory from my stay in Paraguay. I was glad we found it and that we were able to see a bit of Asunción from above. Even though I knew we wouldn’t be doing any trekking in the city, this trip still involved quite a bit of walking and getting a nice view from up high. That’s what I love about less planned trips—the best stories are created along the way ❤️.
Visitar este bar, llamado Guaraní Lounge, fue un buen recuerdo dentro de mi estadía en Paraguay. Me alegré que lo hayamos encontrado y que hayamos podido ver un poco de Asunción desde arriba. Si bien sabía que en la ciudad no haríamos nada de trekking, este viaje tuvo su cuota de caminar bastante y obtener una buena vista desde la altura. Esto es lo que me gusta de los viajes no tan planeados: las mejores anécdotas se van creando sobre la marcha ❤️.

![Kopia – Whispers.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23xyi6ueGf3YuTPgs57te64jf1bjq5n1ifdeDRyucCfQDSQ6Q2k6xmEKHziyJmKzmj9fy.jpg)


As promised earlier, I invite you to another set of frames from HEIDELBERG. This time it won’t be Heidelberg seen from the riverside, but Heidelberg viewed from above.

>Zgodnie ze swoją wcześniejszą obietnicą zapraszam na kolejną odsłonę kadrów z HEIDELBERGU. Tym razem nie będzie to Heidelberg pokazany znad rzeki, a będzie to Heidelberg widziany z góry.

I started my visit to Heidelberg with the famous path SCHLANGENWEG. It is a very well-known walking path leading up the hills on the other side of the Neckar River, opposite the Old Town.
Translated literally the name means “snake path” and refers to its winding, serpentine route. The path begins near the Old Bridge and leads steeply uphill. If I remember correctly the route is about two kilometers long.
I have to admit that it was quite physically demanding for me. In some places it is really steep and at certain points you have to climb up stone steps.

>Swoją wizytę w Heidelbergu rozpoczęłam od słynnej ścieżki "SCHLANGENWEG". Jest to bardzo znana ścieżka spacerowa prowadząca na wzgórza po drugiej stronie rzeki Neckar, naprzeciwko Starego Miasta. Tłumacząc dosłownie nazwa oznacza "wężową ścieżkę" i odnosi się oczywiście do jej serpentyn i krętych ścieżek. Ścieżka ta zaczyna się w pobliżu Starego Mostu, prowadzi stromo pod górę. O ile dobrze pamiętam, trasa wynosi około dwóch kilometrów. Muszę przyznać, że była to trasa dla mnie bardzo wymagająca fizycznie. Miejscami jest tam naprawdę stromo, gdzieniegdzie na górę prowadzą nas kamienne schody.



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23xedt74gBj9xDsAKN5UHtDXtpDbL5i9UHFW7ibRYSA5gZV3Q2gFsoaHbTKWdd3sZtCE1.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23uFTh84RQvqeNWsP2Fhobw6bT69UvzGZg5TmMbQhzy1Ysd3jCj1s7gxuCJw9aLmpnxku.png)


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23wgHutb4wRom93vMsZbWZfNjm4JAtP7SoHXTMt5nqnjKj3Ao9cUsUueWe758nwt4yBqX.png)

Without a doubt the biggest advantage of this walk was the picturesque views. Almost the entire time while climbing up the hill, it was possible to admire the panorama of Heidelberg, the Neckar River and the Old Town.

If you want to see the city from above, with its contrasting rooftops, this is definitely one of the best places in the city.

>Niewątpliwie największą zaletą tego spaceru były malownicze widoki. Praktycznie przez cały czas wspinając się na to wzgórze, można było podziwiać panoramę Heidelbergu, rzekę Neckar oraz stare miasto.
>
>Jeśli chcemy zobaczyć miasto z góry, kontrastowe dachy, to będzie to niewątpliwie jedno z lepszych miejsc w mieście.


![20250726_114753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/EoAYEVTRqve1k4dAf38mVZiPwk6UayviR5ZzKSj6fJbybvDts6km7vgxbu4utwDgmyk.jpg)

![20250726_112647.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/Eou6j4c8tdQuNbipYMM6ED8TRqjyLK4rAPcmz2TZJ2B6Gqe5G1NNSQ4keafmwotuBwq.jpg)

![20250726_130728.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/Eq7LSANesZ4J6EhPcW7iDJD54m1nuetVcMkg4gXXMhY16U4dh1H6N438hN3uuroobMy.jpg)

The most iconic landmark of Heidelberg is, of course, its beautiful castle, also located on a hill. While walking along the Schlangenweg, you can admire the castle from a distance, as it blends perfectly into the surrounding hills.
However I won’t go into detail about the castle today, as it is interesting enough to deserve a separate post.

>Największą wizytówką miasta Heidelberg jest oczywiście jego przepiękny zamek, zlokalizowany również na wzgórzu. Spacerując Schlangenweg możemy również podziwiać zamek z daleka, który pięknie komponuje się ze wzgórzami. Nie będę jednak dzisiaj się rozpisywała na temat tego zamku, gdyż jest on na tyle interesujący, że zasługuje na osobny post.


![20250726_114732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tbiNH2RDswojtQG6rWBhx3SLjet3fKbTKRSerbdPVjhTx59juARyBWzSUK2QmZxv295.jpg)

For the way back I chose a different walking path, which was definitely less demanding. I slightly regretted not doing it the other way around. It would have been much easier to go uphill on an asphalt road and come back via the Schlangenweg.
But as we say in Poland : "a person becomes wise after the damage is done" 😁

>Na drogę powrotną wybrałam inną ścieżkę spacerową, która była zdecydowanie mniej wymagająca. Trochę żałowałam, że nie zrobiłam tego odwrotnie. O wiele łatwiej byłoby wspinać się na górę drogą asfaltową, a wracać Schlangenweg. No ale jest takie przysłowie w Polsce : "Polak mądry po szkodzie" 😁


![20250726_113303.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tSL9RaRbuZS7QEREYAsiSrkosdzfzBk8oTwjFM6pJKSKcn8YoQNd6azcBBwfprH6MVK.jpg)

---
*The photo above is my entry for #aroundtheworld contest*

---

![20250726_130745.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23u5vxcXfXTBLMZbRaWCLG2tgL3phaihxUL2T6NEonjWobE1nvXtVPaUoUAgzQSbXcPDF.jpg)

![20250726_114021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tvW8xFHtEPQZ3Vha23EyCN4ysBNRQ5cR98PDLiYan1uyA7ce7CBUbJipCPEkSr8Uokf.jpg)

After this exhausting walk I headed towards the castle. As I mentioned earlier, photos of the castle will appear on my profile another day. The castle is very large and very interesting, so I took a lot of photos.

Today, however, I would like to share with you the view I found on the hill where the castle is located. It is another place in Heidelberg where you can admire the view of the Old Town, directly from above.

From this point you could clearly see the dense urban layout of Heidelberg. What also caught my attention were the red rooftops. Almost all the buildings were in the same color, which created a very pleasing composition.

>Po tym wyczerpującym spacerze udałam się w stronę zamku. Jak już wcześniej wspomniałam zdjęcia zamku pojawią się innego dnia na moim profilu. Zamek jest bardzo duży i bardzo ciekawy. Zrobiłam bardzo dużo zdjęć, a dzisiaj chciałabym podzielić się z wami widokiem, który zastałam na wzgórzu, na którym jest zlokalizowany zamek. 
>
>Jest to kolejne miejsce w Heidelbergu, w którym można podziwiać widok bezpośredio na Stare Miasto. Z góry doskonale było widać zwartą zabudowę miasta Heidelbergu. Moją uwagę również zwróciły czerwone dachy. Praktycznie wszystkie budynki były w tym samym kolorze, co świetnie się to komponowało.


![20250726_130810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23vhsGMLuXSbq7WVCu2iXXTCGnvdCVSh7wRMjKiftmgQG8RWWHK9WVCaXki7Tmj1ABT5A.jpg)

In the panorama of Heidelberg one building stood out in particular — the CHURCH OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. It is one of the most important and characteristic buildings in Heidelberg. It is located in the very heart of the Old Town, right by the market square and is the largest church in the city. It was built mainly in the Gothic style between the 14th and 16th centuries.

>W panoramie Heidelbergu szczególnie wyróżniał się jeden budynek, a mianowicie KOŚCIÓŁ DUCHA ŚWIĘTEGO. Jest to jeden z najważniejszych i najbardziej charakterystycznych budynków w Heidelbergu. Znajduje się w samym sercu Starego Miasta, tuż przy rynku i jest największym kościołem w mieście. Został zbudowany głównie w stylu gotyckim między XIV a XVI wiekiem.


![20250726_131021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tvVvYsgsXAB952ZUAEZuPwcfGvYRF8bRx79Q3gFvh5HP5hsQxVzXHEEwrRMs7p2KSYR.jpg)

![20250726_130957.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23y8mWM7UvbtBG8xePmJMjuc3Ye2kXed4aUEGk8d3mYJ2LBZbTGtnE64Z2b3WYoLYNW18.jpg)


It was another successful weekend on the road. I’m already looking forward to more weekends like this.🤗

![662938943_1506201641068370_7767304517247518609_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EowGaTvHGttti5sdip4cE48gBjLPkSCNmpQUCWbbKFvyfniA1S7WZRggAqq9rTz6HUk.jpg)
>These porticoes recall the prayer of the Rosary

One of the things I like to do when I go to discover new cities is to find panoramic points from where I can admire the city from above, one of these is the square of the sanctuary of Monte Berico in Vicenza, but to get to this place you have to pass through these porticos, and it is always a beautiful route to do on foot, even if a little tiring.


![664703144_1506201684401699_8128667411592208853_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EpLg1mfNvqhRkm38ty8gGy5yDRiwT6Q6DS9ewRS6VTEDxXwTcF3g2A2ZdgefChKY5XW.jpg)

I recommend this route to all tourists who come to visit the city of Vicenza, and I recommend you do it on foot because in this way you can admire these beautiful Porticoes that were built between 1746 and 1780 based on a project by a very famous architect who built many villas in Vicenza and I'm talking about Francesco Muttoni, think that these Porticoes took about 30 years to build and they are about 700 meters long.


![668146418_1506202004401667_5283894671382745299_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/EpVC9YnhjB1ofW8u4bmAYQ1sZ2NGwmAiQcGRMvT4JgCDE8oYHpy4mNsunivwc393d3H.jpg)
>I must say that the facade of this sanctuary is truly beautiful

but when you get to the end of this beautiful path, you find yourself in front of the sanctuary of the Madonna di Monte Berico, a sanctuary that was built around 1400 and is still today a super destination for pilgrims, because it is said that here there was an apparition of the Madonna.


![666016296_1506202607734940_9215688371819503958_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/243WVpHKs3gbo1eGpXjSki9AUtTXMqz9Y1W9LTcvQ9ADZBMKDqY2dUbRyb5cfsuHRPNL3.jpg)

![663050956_1506202511068283_1349021377297952876_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/241ZrPxjRTbyRMKCKw8WBjPx4rnFva7XYK3oyfqqG7ACfXscMvuMhcin6t1Ad9CFWFiDy.jpg)

Yesterday, I didn't have so much time to visit the Basilica which I have already visited several times but I invite you, perhaps as tourists, to visit it because there are many very interesting works, among the best Italian painters, but more than anything what I recommend you do is to admire Vicenza from above from this square, if you are lucky as I was, you can see a beautiful panorama of the whole city of Vicenza.


![663328798_1506203097734891_7927843336204818803_n.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/244eGbhFWQZMX1rbjZqv2HoT2bYTtuucZ3GxkJQ3YrzbrjSEopXuJGWpLLFJGxy7tfFXH.jpg)
>Outside the museum there are some weapons used during the First World War on display

then if you are nearby, and you want to visit a nice museum, there is the museum of the Risorgimento of the Resistance at Villa Guiccioli, you can do an in-depth study of the local history practically from the Risorgimento to the resistance, if I'm not mistaken this museum should be completely free, I only visited in a beautiful park from where a beautiful cycle/pedestrian path starts which practically takes you back down towards the city of Vicenza.


![foto selfie.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/butterfly-jt9/23wWuGZBX86ynE4J2Y9iyNih47DUPC9qumqMUjPFyAH7bwW3jas4PVmyq62Jsp6fzELLb.jpg)

I must say that it is always so nice to come to these places, where they are rich in history and art but above all there are still these parks where you can walk along these paths and breathe some clean air, a piece of advice that I will definitely give you if you come to visit the city of Vicenza, I thank you for reading and I will see you next time

![cedeño.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23wC9zpYrBR1qhS1d5QDQv1Qi9vza5SLWQFJfdDKn8Qf1ovvZ5hKM8MyPm7ckC7YyVKQv.png)
**
INGLÉS
** Continuing our tour of Cedeño, after crossing the bridge and several streams we saw along the way, we headed towards the lower part of Cedeño. This town is characterized by its location at the foot of the mountain, which affords it a beautiful view. Some houses are located on the upper slopes of the mountain, allowing for a very pleasant climate at night, with a comfortable temperature. During our visit, we arrived at a friend's house, and coincidentally, her house is one of those located on the highest part of the mountain. It has stone steps, and from below, the view is spectacular. The house looks like a small fortress with the mountain in the background. Upon arrival, we organized our backpacks, packed our food, and gathered all the necessary supplies for our stay in Cedeño. This visit wouldn't be complete without trying the traditional wood-fired soup, also known as sancocho. After chatting with the homeowner and listening to her many amusing anecdotes, we set about preparing the meal. After cooking and enjoying a delicious soup, we rested, and around 11:00 AM, we began our trek to the river. We've visited it several times before, and it always had a strong current and a moderate flow, but this time, due to the dry season, it was literally dry. There were areas where only rocks and stagnant water were visible. I never imagined seeing the river like this. The number of rocks in the riverbed was impressive. I spent several minutes observing the rocks and processing how the river had changed with the dry season. The landscape looked different, and I missed the sound of the water, which used to be so inviting.
**
ESPAÑOL
** Continuando nuestro recorrido por Cedeño, tras cruzar el puente y varios arroyos que vimos en el camino, nos dirigimos hacia la parte baja del pueblo. Este se caracteriza por su ubicación al pie de la montaña, lo que le brinda una hermosa vista. Algunas casas se encuentran en las laderas superiores, lo que permite un clima muy agradable por la noche, con una temperatura confortable. Durante nuestra visita, llegamos a la casa de una amiga, y casualmente, su casa es una de las que se ubican en la parte más alta de la montaña. Tiene escalones de piedra y, desde abajo, la vista es espectacular. La casa parece una pequeña fortaleza con la montaña de fondo. Al llegar organizamos los morrales, los la comida y todos los implementos necesarios para nuestra estadía en Cedeño, en esta visita no faltar la tradicional sopa en leña, también conocido como sancocho, luego de conversar con la dueña de la casa y escuchar sus divertidas anécdotas, que tiene muchas por cierto, nos dispusimos a preparar la comida, luego de preparar la comida y disfrutar una deliciosa sopa, descansamos y aproximadamente a las 11 de la mañana iniciamos nuestro recorrido hacia el río, lo hemos visitado en varias oportunidades y siempre tenía un caudal abundante y corriente moderada, pero esta vez nos sorprendió, por la temporada de sequía, está literalmente seco, hay áreas donde solo se observan rocas y agua estancada, nunca imaginé ver el río así, la cantidad de rocas que tiene en el lecho es impresionante, estuve varios minutos observando las rocas y procesando como el río había cambiado con la estación seca, el paisaje se ve diferente y extrañé el sonido del agua, que invitaba a bañarse.
![río seco (6).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EnqSaemW6e3krRc8okAv2La22hnaZWzetjweyXPp5PFi4KkjeAFHr9KsnTxi6eRFuRL.jpeg) ![río seco (4).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Eqd8RTmMZ72uMMoFi1T5pQDd3GNCwdWBkmhwTBFbak3GdXB1w7ExboeaAt7HxVcJNrF.jpeg) ![río seco (5).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Epdh8Ps9JDUPNb174NeoPA9hbGnidNQhrUbFbNK7N5EFRXfX3Az1xNWqvjPhMGJA49X.jpeg) ![río seco (14).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23zkfkMovmoAezLSBq7bztXw9fZpVieKXLjWXkRGigUDnUCet4qDPQdjSDLsjcExwFwua.jpeg) ![río seco (9).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23ywqBWUo9z7FA2JHo3ENHspgpscr12hkxkAjNrYwwNmnp8aWSN48MtAp6DbgvKKBGqo3.jpeg) ![río seco (13).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/2458J8cE1VZJx6PWjviSrSKeBJE1MQaitVUsfncdDwAJ8arp8hFwcCyEcjwjSfZSx76xA.jpeg) ![río seco (12).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23wqpNUGHu5k5GkED9PchoqJYdibVKxDgd9x3ED6m9MdkKUvPMcUwkofHHQrLKjJ3UBnY.jpeg) ![río seco (11).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EpLf6vTzDMw8YoXpQ2izBLQPqBkKfVTTTNra3eB2z5wmk6fQNwH36r8gzCfLbQg5SKn.jpeg) ![río seco (7).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23wWtxZN1jYUYWS36qKp6JvMqMYwQhV9ypE8GE4usmKEkiVQJpF5HiuF8H3xmzUG46Ga8.jpeg) ![río seco (8).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23z7DmtWxkX6R9i7Gjo7P5xe5GAK2T7Girkiq6LhJLzmbptdXLAWGchztzKQmFC7cGS8P.jpeg) ![río seco (10).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/23zkiUux9g1B2KkkiBVJLDL1dz43jfiL7kvLKM4LJM9T1KmTNoTVg8iUXDEW24HzvSDmu.jpeg)
Our mission was to swim and cool off in the river. Seeing several dry areas, I was a little discouraged, but with Mrs. Ely's help, we continued up the path in search of other pools she knew very well. The view along the way was beautiful, and according to her, the water was cold, ideal for a refreshing swim. The rocky path was somewhat difficult, especially for the children, so we decided to leave the rocky path and walk alongside the river on small dirt trails, dry branches, and trees. This shortcut allowed us to reach the deeper pools, determined to enjoy a refreshing swim. The dirt path was easier than I thought; just be careful of the thorny plants and move slowly through the slippery sand. The trail had some inclines, and the sun was a bit strong at that time of day. The rest of the journey, following the routine of walking slowly and being careful of the plants and thorns, went by quickly, and we finally arrived at the pool. When I saw it, I loved it: crystal-clear water, abundant flow, and several round rocks that we used as pillows to lie down and enjoy the cool water. A natural tub surrounded by vegetation, with the mountain on one side.
Nuestra misión era bañarnos y refrescarnos en el río, al ver varias zonas secas, me desanimé un poco pero con ayuda de la señora Ely, seguimos el sendero hacia arriba en busca de otras pozas que ella conoce muy bien, la vista del camino es bonita y según su explicación con agua fría, ideal para darnos un refrescante baño, el camino por las piedras fue un tanto difícil sobre todo para los niños, por ello decidimos salir del camino de rocas y caminar bordeando el río por pequeños senderos de tierra, ramas secas y árboles, este atajo nos permitió avanzar hasta las pozas más profundas, firmes en nuestro objetivo de disfrutar un refrescante baño. El camino de tierra fue más sencillo de lo que pensé, solo tener cuidado con las plantas de espinas y movilizarse despacio por la arena, es resbaladiza, el sendero con algunas inclinaciones y por la hora el sol estaba un poco fuerte, el resto del trayecto siguiendo la rutina de caminar despacio cuidándose de las plantas y los pinchazos se hizo rápido y llegamos finalmente a la poza, al verla me encantó, el agua cristalina, abundante caudal y varias rocas redondas que usamos como almohada para acostarnos y disfrutar el agua fresca, una tina natural rodeada de vegetación y a un lado la montaña.
![río seco (18).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Eqd91ZYKm1oEPXhYqAZyPoZQ9rMRmwdy1uvUCh6wHsuv4KTAinjEv83U6wD6G84g2UB.jpeg) ![río seco (22).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EoGyQ3urb3B4UCkTb7QGcvF1pw4d7gaj3e17TDaXeKPGL6rSVhH49cb7zYQGfXsCEm3.jpeg) ![río seco (28).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EoTeNpHpZQibUP9U9w8s327QXJMY3dbJiZTZ2Lo9HQKydv3zBvTTHBnBDcHom1KZu8r.jpeg) ![río seco (33).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EpEGGxCEz5hhvnTqhvKcgTgtUhYit2h3w1TbUWqHQWMr3PzFFsatwfeeuZHBNgA6GPg.jpeg) ![río seco (25).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EoyNxnpp5GbLa4f8LoWoxCBkbG6syiAoJA12LWVEHHttPhGaPu43QhDimH57Zijuoei.jpeg) ![río seco (34).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EppKhuckky8FfZ5XqAe8syGhYS3uWprzaCcUZUvW4ae6xZEdeN4PafVyENuyqEjuVG4.jpeg) ![río seco (19).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EpxrCt7pshmcXkf6jDXEhXgVJBFyLXHiPULWhnGfZvsJA8DCWxgMrLSTqyNU18Nf1YB.jpeg) ![río seco (30).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EnmDf3sUr43AhqmK7v39XUc9yAAVYMgTzSzXML6JW6KMYrCVCK8mScuMLJKFFQqT1B1.jpeg) ![río seco (21).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EqNEfxtsJo949UY4oGR2Map8DE6Dru3wpVVn2MBuh7fqHKqWNXRYiWy6736AzmmFKoL.jpeg) ![río seco (29).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EogLvs9Jy5JGcbvfJJxaiJUL7N5P3v8qjQSvMBcXaGXm3her7eAnaskxijyn1PEjg1N.jpeg)
This pool was a true oasis after our hike in search of a place to swim. The water was crystal clear, and the mountain view was incredible. I loved the scenery. The children, as usual, were the first to want to swim, but first, an adult checked the river's depth and identified the safest areas for them to swim safely. After the exploration, the children went for a swim, and when we left, they didn't want to get out. I understand why, because the water was just right and perfect for a refreshing dip. It was still early, so we decided to head to another pool recommended by Mrs. Ely. This one is located a little further upstream. The path is made up of rocks that are part of a dry section of the river, but the trail didn't stop us from continuing on and swimming. The view is spectacular, and you can see some rocks, the trees reflected in the water, and the sun's rays, which were gradually getting stronger. But none of this deterred us from continuing on to the next pool. Compared to the previous one, I must say that this one was wider and the water clearer. Here we stopped for about 3 hours, swimming, playing, splashing, walking, and exploring several meters of the area towards the right bank of the river. There are several cultivated areas located around the mountain; some of the crops grown there are pineapple, yucca, corn, among others. We also saw some pack donkeys transporting the produce from the mountain to the houses located several kilometers from the river. I liked this part of the mountain because, although it's in the dry season, it remains relatively green, perhaps due to its proximity to the river, which maintains a constant flow of water. This helps preserve the abundant vegetation with its varied shades of green, creating a beautiful landscape. In several photographs, you can see the view of the mountain, its reflection in the river, and the sun's rays increasing as the day progresses. After several hours in the river, swimming, and playing, we returned home with the lady to rest and continue our journey the next day.
Esta poza fue verdadero oasis luego de nuestra caminata en búsqueda de un espacio para bañarnos, el agua es cristalina y con una vista increíble de la montaña , este paisaje me encantó, los niños como siempre suelen hacerlo, fueron los primeros en querer bañarse, pero antes, un adulto se encargó de verificar la profundidad del río y cuáles eran las zonas más apropiadas para que los niños pudiesen bañarse tranquilamente, terminada la exploración los niños se bañaron y al momento de venirnos no querían salirse del agua y los entiendo porque estaba en su punto y perfecta para un refrescante baño. Aún era temprano y decidimos avanzar hacia otra poza que nos recomendó la señora Ely, está se ubica un poco más arriba, el camino está formado por rocas que corresponden a la parte seca de un tramo del río, el sendero no fue impedimento para para avanzar hasta allá y aprovechar para seguir bañándonos, la vista es espectacular y se alcanzan a observar algunas rocas, los árboles reflejados en el agua y los rayos del sol que aumentaban progresivamente, pero no impidieron nuestro avance para conocer la siguiente poza; en comparación con la anterior, debo decir que esta era más amplia y el agua más cristalina, aquí hicimos una parada de aproximadamente 3 horas, nos bañamos, jugamos chapoteamos, caminamos y recorrimos varios metros de la zona, hacia el margen derecho del río, hay varias zonas de cultivo ubicadas alrededor de la montaña, algunos de los rubros que se cultivan son piña, yuca, maíz, entre otros, también observamos algunos burros de carga transportando los frutos desde la montaña hasta las casas ubicadas a varios kilómetros del río, esta parte de la montaña me gustó porque aunque está en el período de sequía, se conserva relativamente verde, tal vez por la cercanía al río que mantiene un curso permanente de agua, le ayuda a conservar la abundante vegetación con variados tonos verdes, formando un hermoso paisaje, en varias fotografías se aprecia la vista de la montaña, su reflejo en el río y los rayos solares incrementando a medida que avanza el día, luego de varias horas en el río, bañarnos y jugar volvimos a casa con la señora para descansar y continuar nuestra jornada el día siguiente.
![río seco (20).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/244xnxM3DhAxS7YTHKEWr4ZWzpbcmgnVU6dNsHJ75HoPacp3w6BRJdAeHNBZuUY6C3Sdf.jpeg) ![río seco (23).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EnWJueVZf365zzqXT8Q4HGZX7dHKkwrQCU2KhyM77jLVfKTwXzzw32ZvP4N6YW1gz8c.jpeg) ![río.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Eos1o4b2xF8ukckYr2dQeDnPCDTNHwLbAuQW7qGWz6foVSZgJ1JBqfvFSPBbg4o3gK2.png) ![río seco (17).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EqUcSCHwq7WbKCKabS4S8WJJfYJPZsjoShgHHanGRWMH7sCmCERWMB3cPQCtf5NxtWE.jpeg) ![río seco (15).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EoMDfLVfudsR9pExBC3759iBJ2M7d5a9ZCXgUx318tFhfsGEYuZ1hDp78bvWo1W1k7o.jpeg) ![río seco (3).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/EpNos5hwdpyu8VYVYJv2Fnadh86mCb5saq7rLJnaLsrQSpHxgBmzyggdNt7jiDwTQzD.jpeg) ![río seco (27).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Eq9TN9YxV33WRvVD99prG6iyPXDqUoV9ccHNGRtwygw6V3meLD2yqpvobymQnfUw41d.jpeg) ![río seco (24).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Eq9UPh9TrEBhhEi2FL8myuMkVSdHWNYGjfruZ7jUyyBZQ6Ho6hTkAM8echWe3CsSWsK.jpeg) ![río seco (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belkyscabrera/Ep5o4ynkE4fRbtHTUJbRSwrJyxQm4GkMYTeyV7jodPsKtxyKHnkMR6C1bnwE7sCbWJ9.jpeg)

# A Backdoor into the Arches

I don't know any of you visited some of the popular National parks in 2025-26, due to budget cuts, a lot of the facilities are currently restricted. Many parks, including Arches National Park had "timed entry" in 2025. Thankfully in 2026 it is taken away again, so just like before you can enter the Park at any time in 2026. I was there with my family over the Easter weekend for a short trip. Arches National Park can feel overwhelming at first—crowded entrances, long lines of cars, and packed parking lots. For our recent trip, we decided to do things differently. Instead of joining the line at the main entrance, we rented a Jeep Wrangler Rubicon 4WD and entered the park through the Willow Springs Trail, a lesser‑known backcountry route. It ended up being one of the highlights of the entire trip—especially for our kids.


![IMG_5246.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EqqusuD6fjqjKcCnCwkTxWLRjZihFoWKpFJnNsrqsA1obDi1wW1uNJ8zuj1Qvz4gWp4.jpeg)


# Willow Springs Trail

One thing worth mentioning upfront is that finding the entrance to Willow Springs Trail is not straightforward anymore. The old, direct access from Highway 191 (to BLM road 378) —which many older maps and blog posts still reference—is now blocked. You can’t simply turn off the highway and drive straight onto Willow Springs Road like you used to.


![IMG_5154.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq7KXRc5KyivnM1q6T88SrB2QUoo63bQbWowFKYxKZ2qHX3jW19ZVBjPNoT8k4AdQ3y.jpeg)




Today, the only practical way to access Willow Springs Trail is through the newly created Utahraptor State Park entrance. This initially caused some confusion for us, because it feels like you’re entering a state park just to get to the trail.

![IMG_5149.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EpJWFx4xLa73fKBM5JWAnr6dioLqZPYnRHTaCspVTYfPy7QTFwuzbudKgdS8av5FuN4.jpeg)

The good news—and this is important—is that you do not need to pay the Utahraptor State Park fee if you are only transiting through to access Willow Springs Trail. There’s no separate booth for Willow Springs itself, and as long as you’re just driving through to reach the Arches backcountry route, there’s no additional charge. That was a relief to confirm before heading in.

Navigation-wise, signage can still feel a bit sparse, so having an offline map or GPS track helps. Once you’re on the correct dirt road, though, it’s obvious—you’re heading straight into wide‑open desert with sandstone fins rising on both sides.

# Trail Details

Willow Springs Trail is not technical off‑roading, but it’s real 4WD driving. Sandy washes, slickrock sections, mild ledges, and washboard surfaces kept things interesting, and the Rubicon handled it effortlessly. For the kids, every bump and dip was a thrill. They called it “desert roller‑coaster mode,” and every sandy section came with laughter and excited commentary from the back seat.



![IMG_5147.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Ep5kMCBJtnXJoR78WUy2kB2Yuav3HirHmAZctNN1PXvHepJMA5aPtr7aem2Jk6UkzQu.jpeg)

One of the best parts of this route is how quiet it feels. With the windows down, we could hear the wind, the crunch of tires on gravel, and the occasional shout of excitement when the Jeep climbed over rock ledges. We stopped briefly to explore the dinosaur track area along the road—a bonus that added a paleontological layer to the adventure.


![IMG_5135.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq355Dsm5otAwYetVH8k8FMztK8NZmN1JB7w3yqCM3iYAVqJk1puKnrp3zjTxnNBXUW.jpeg)

There are Dinosaurs footprints to look at along the way. I have been able to show the kids both Theropod and Sauropod prints.


![IMG_5140.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/23tbwM7DQGN41qLuBsjG8y6imzmhoZVp7Phhwi8WGiGiyQVfTLqkBu6R9rvyqMSkp3Pkm.jpeg)


![IMG_5137.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EoGxrqkLYAQFLF8VbdyZfQjZJBMp5KwszfS4bQbJTBeiGf8vkjzaNw3UvhBFd6ennaZ.jpeg)


After roughly eight miles, the dirt road suddenly met pavement. Just like that, we popped out near the Balanced Rock parking area, officially inside Arches National Park—without waiting in a single line.

# Devils Garden and Landscape Arch

From Balanced Rock, we joined the main park road and drove straight to Devils Garden, knowing it gets busy later in the day. Getting there earlier felt like a small victory after our quiet backcountry entry.

We parked, pulled out our packed lunch, and claimed a shaded picnic table. Eating lunch surrounded by towering sandstone fins and spires is one of those small moments that sticks with you—and it gave the kids a well‑timed energy reset before hiking.

The hike to Landscape Arch is ideal for families. The trail is well maintained, mostly flat, and full of interesting rock formations that kept the kids engaged. They ran ahead, stopped to inspect rocks, and asked a steady stream of questions about how arches form—questions we answered with varying degrees of geological confidence:) Kidding! My wife did her PhD here in the Arches and Canyonlands, and we have many field seasons together here. Kids are often overwhelmed with our constant chatter, in a good way!


![IMG_5186.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq7KycyM53BqAkPVeGhf6qz94vDVuw1ySM3zKTDLyFCRfmwRwgv9YtbTYCmrHERrzRh.jpeg)



Standing beneath Landscape Arch is humbling. The span is unbelievably long and thin, and seeing it in person makes you appreciate just how delicate it really is. We lingered, took photos, and enjoyed one of those rare quiet moments where even the kids paused to stare.


![IMG_5180.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Ep7tCPSeTQXeby3Qyx6HPnggaHet5u69pcjM8nn5yQz9c9HDoDhoHFyuCETd9DfET8J.jpeg)



# Sunset at Delicate Arch (not quite, but close)

After Devils Garden, we spent the afternoon driving through the heart of the park, stopping at viewpoints before heading toward Delicate Arch later in the day. Timing this hike closer to sunset was intentional—and absolutely worth it.

![IMG_5224.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EogMtF6bsoKBLhpfbggDanc9A5GrLQMngvqtP64cbQWRxV7vHXqGRBvZ8JuvfUeME29.jpeg)

The Delicate Arch trail is more demanding, especially with kids. There’s steady elevation gain, exposed slickrock, and very little shade. But the trail is visually engaging the entire way, and the anticipation keeps everyone moving.



![IMG_5234.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EpA26qyAAtM7TJa5AwXbJNT8kbRzMNGrHESdKabSEYf99Rxi2uXiyjYNMHuiAeTPGiC.jpeg)

There are couple of smaller arches nearby along the trail which kids enjoyed at lot more, as they were free of crowds and they could do whatever they wanted over there.

![IMG_5253.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EopqUGMh61WWfhBEr9xgZxtS889mAop3wmDvZRE7uHnVyuQYRp13pqZ3vMtpgzbsZYH.jpeg)




As the sun dropped lower, the colors of the rock deepened—reds shifting to orange, shadows stretching across the bowls and fins. When we finally rounded the last corner and Delicate Arch came into view, the kids nearly forgot how tired they were. We didn't stay up all the way to sunset, which is 7:40pm, because then we would have to get down in the dark. I didn't want to do that with kids, so we left around 6 pm and got down in about 45 min to our car.






# Why This Day Worked So Well

Entering Arches via Willow Springs Trail set the tone for the entire visit. It wasn’t just about skipping the lines—it was about turning the drive itself into an adventure. The off‑road experience engaged the kids from the start and made them feel like part of the journey, not just passengers heading to the next stop.

Combining that with iconic hikes—Landscape Arch for awe and ease, Delicate Arch for challenge and drama—made it feel like a perfectly balanced day: adventure, hiking, family time, and unforgettable scenery.

If you’re visiting Arches with kids and want a more memorable, hands‑on experience than the standard park entry, renting a 4WD and using Willow Springs Trail is absolutely worth considering. For us, it turned a crowded national park into a personal adventure—and gave the kids a day that they will remember.

![Straight out of Amsterdam.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tbnPUUgB6jd14VqddPmvsiStpF94HMKmBxX39eX8VikKjMeocpKmkKjmywiCB8MEc3r.jpg)

<center>

In the heart of the city, is a street, not a very long street, probably less than 300yds in fact. But what a feast of German Art Nouveau, or "Jugendstil" architecture. Lets gaze upwards as we walk Albert Street, Riga.  

![_DSC3356.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/Eoni9t5ajeUCGQxk4837PLNyNiCbS9G1cmhQTMLDAP11XXuXoRag9nUkywLuyNx4NiU.jpg)

Riga was founded in 1201, by Albert of Riga, a catholic bishop, in 1901 in celebration of 700 years of existence construction of the street commenced and was completed in 1908.

![_DSC3359.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23xVAR7Lf6b5w6FJeYkFCXKRWdeqP1pzKA9449PzHESMWLRfgGNPkrtUPkdMUHp8rUb5V.jpg)

The art-nouveau museum

![_DSC3366.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tkk13c51fCNibK7ZhUKr4sU6wuXPBtYX2WNzYi2S7gKFv5SmcggFGddMZRFHuiSE8rR.jpg)

and its ornate staircase


![_DSC3360.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tm9Fs3oCUGaCiANy8RFEoXRUGQLzS8mQd44KuMAfESXWJ8uzAsWpgemcENqLguvQsaG.jpg)

  








![_DSC3367.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tH1RbHgTwE6BXPLM4rQxZSwwkx1KGZyfYVuGLW1ikMkGkduVHW7JyHbW4CQiHaPJSxL.jpg)

![_DSC3368.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tmFdyGg6STgro1JA6CHcjiGavrAsKNyxp6urCQKdpufidiAki49exQQYnWxK8xgRJ8S.jpg)

Albert Street was "erased" from Riga's memory when in 1941, as part of an effort to erase pre-Soviet identity and history. the Soviets renamed it Friča Gaiļa Street, he being a communist activist, arrested by the Latvians for carrying out illegal political actions taken to No 13, the home of the Political Police Department, where on the evening of 4th January 1933 he died under mysterious circumstances, thrown out of a fourth floor window in a staged "apparent suicide." 

![_DSC3345.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/2432Bm45PfANRtjbEdLWLPDgX6FyZHnwsa1oHWr7fuKSFov8HpnpAGNNBqqZug5dTTUjr.jpg) A silver willy

![_DSC3348.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/Eo45qnRXB4xWpD95UVmdMHTRDrzWmbx7zd9V3fuH7DFd4gpHeCVj86uTvu8jt63Stcp.jpg)

Between 1942-44 when Latvia was occupied by Germany it was renamed Hollanderu Strasse, with good old Friča Gaiļa making his comeback with the Soviet reoccupation.

![_DSC3349.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23wC5GS7gSWrUyGC1QvB1jX83LZESZJQf2Uvp5teetgLSe9hV8v2p74rMET1wMdEYd8b4.jpg)

![_DSC3354 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23vhyeYGT2NstBtQ5Pt26uams4QQCekLJSrr6F5y5GeVFm6Y6VuWgWfd6stqkC8BANJjc.jpg)

![_DSC3354.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23uFRQX3jau6hBoqHcUHZpJE6CdwxjW2mnizeLTswHMQ3gjoNjx9XssNi3qhgbSqDVZ2X.jpg)

For 50 years Albert Street fell into disrepair, *"The problem with communism is that if nothing belongs to nobody, nobody takes care of it".*

![_DSC3357.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23w2covgq9p1rijBmmJb9ntHCVbky1eaBPy288hyWRQM7ivRjxzyZ6Kh1bzqUCheBMPpT.jpg)

![_DSC3358.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tGVute1gojZwTzE5gFsPxWqtmxcygLAFi9rEBHspEoxWxcBRJvCqBjssogYUheQ3bTk.jpg)

![_DSC3389.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23uQkSFFyLN5BXAFR694jYZ4kEY3cjPoUDrWaDpGJJnaNFkyaupCGGPc8e6K5Bo1hxEDD.jpg)

Finally with the break up of the USSR, Alberta Street was again renamed. The buildings, are now a UNESCO World Heritage site, having undergone extensive restoration to return them to their former grandeur and glory, 

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23swXqJXt8Mc6TXJwmnAwmv4oMxoBwAjmvRLoXcDDUHEhxE4HEypbBti31EAuDAcFEBWt.png

![_DSC3346.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tvW4bjfhkrhRGnUej6PLcVT86oaCFLyL4rj3oCCF7vsiLYPyu7RE4gzoH1ikQhXvVPK.jpg) Nice 

![_DSC3350.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/grindle/23tbkSJruGWCwoD3g1P2h8Gx4PmP1qeuHsfv79AF3osX6MKx9ZgBQouaw76QXrYKe25HH.jpg) Nicer

![1_20260408_141231_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23tvgEiyB93vXi7QvLpaQwgL5jGin4EbpsrpXsxbpiX7DzTfZgLMD3aoBp3kGWwVTzuY7.png)


We went to Eliberta Spring Resort located in Zamboanga. It was such an exciting trip because i was with my siblings. As soon as we arrived i was amazed by how beautiful the place is. It is surrounded by so many tall trees and green plants. The air feels so fresh and cool even before you touch the water. It really feels like you are in the middle of nature far away from the busy city.
 

![9_20260408_141232_0008.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23w2gc5eGkaN1FyLaEkmaHUjRSTpNTAMLkDxwsVbbayuQNfAzGJDgzcMuKEYiQNgvgesg.png)

The first thing i noticed was the water. Oh my goodness the water is so cold! It is not just a little bit cold, it is extremely cold. When i dipped my feet in i immediately shivered. It feels like ice water coming straight from the ground. It is the kind of cold that wakes you up instantly. Even though it was hot outside the water stayed so cold and refreshing the whole time we were there.
 


![8_20260408_141232_0007.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23u5vRrFdcYxz55X8iJGzcdaWYiWrHGTTpZpMoxjfNnZqoBt2RYDLeXit85DoyNtBgmV4.png)


Being with my brothers and sisters made everything so much fun. We were all laughing and shouting because of the cold water. At first nobody wanted to jump in first because it was too freezing! We were teasing each other pushing one another playfully just to see who would go in first. The atmosphere was full of joy and noise exactly how family bonding should be.
 

![7_20260408_141232_0006.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23w2eoy5ZrWUxj4vraTvTWU14vWMu7XhnUtSZBrMEsMvKT8XtVajU5gRvK2FxiHq3e4ep.png)

The resort has these amazing man made waterfalls. The water flows down smoothly and looks so pretty. The pools are big and clean and you can see the water clearly. The design of the place is really nice because it looks natural. It does not look like a fake pool it blends perfectly with the trees and rocks around it. Every corner is beautiful and perfect for taking pictures.
 

![6_20260408_141232_0005.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23tveJRY7buAULVTvBda2YCMjPC1Eem4RXfvpGrWxEeiracpHmLX1Lqo9LDptcsp9agtf.png)

We spent a lot of time swimming and just soaking in the water. Even though it was super cold it felt so good on our skin. It made us feel so alive and awake. We swam together from one side to the other. Sometimes we would just float and relax looking up at the trees above us. The sound of the water flowing is very relaxing and peaceful to listen to.
 

![5_20260408_141232_0004.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23z7BYErZwWNNEgiPQUEcfzWDEBeZVHqZPJrymi6Z9wi6V2QoUp9DWZLyHvcRqS7GNAfZ.png)

There are also nice spots where you can sit and rest. They have tables and benches made to look like big tree stumps. They are very unique and fit the vibe of the place. When we got tired from swimming we sat there to dry off a bit and catch our breath. It was nice to just sit down talk and watch other people enjoying the water too.
 

![4_20260408_141232_0003.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23uQjuwRttYrXTtYxzX82whWukRtvYUb4ayu3QrDGmHERnseima3whyCDtDzwxLZbH1Fi.png)

The whole place is very green and shady because of the big trees. You don’t feel the heat of the sun too much because the leaves cover you. It feels comfortable staying there the whole day. The environment is very clean and well maintained. You can really see that they take good care of the resort so that visitors will enjoy and come back again.
 

![3_20260408_141232_0002.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23wqbuHj7t9Hn4P9c6PYRjoEt28qPuHbdoRLqe8RtZVUufc7RikRUfp9YxRHDtVE4DvQC.png)

We did so many silly things together. We were splashing water at each other and playing around. My siblings and i created so many happy memories that day. It is moments like this that i will never forget. Even though the water was freezing cold our hearts were warm because we were together and having a great time.
 

![2_20260408_141232_0001.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23wgCxftjfEtCUNUU6xwWhMLJnQQxbeVHmTuL4ewgMtxazoc7fVo2FujVr2epPkSgSwNd.png)

The water is really the star of the show here. It is famous for being very cold and it is true! It is the kind of cold that stays in your body even after you get out. It feels so refreshing and it really takes away the tiredness. If you love cold spring water this place is definitely a paradise for you. It is one of the coolest places I have ever been to.
 

![11_20260408_141233_0010.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23vsNUUe52fgu3B85KhgvT93HjraLG7LL2qMX5W4BsfGVJEad6tkMXkN4kaYN294RhEAy.png)

Zamboanga has so many beautiful places, and Eliberta Spring Resort is definitely one of them. It is a perfect destination for family outings or trips with friends. The combination of the beautiful nature, the clean pools and the super cold water is just perfect. We enjoyed every single second of our stay there and we did not want to leave yet.
 

![10_20260408_141233_0009.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/serram007/23tbqC32EW9VYD8ARiRC9ys4EzbnqXabqPCoe7cbZ2JoqycodcD1JfkB6EH98aefeSWME.png)

When it was time to go home we were all tired but very happy. Our bodies felt refreshed and relaxed. Going to Eliberta Spring Resort with my siblings was an awesome experience. If you are planning to travel you should definitely visit here. It is cold it is beautiful and it is a place full of good vibes and happy memories.
